title: Mary Pickford's birth chart
metaDescription: Mary Pickford's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 19.3° Aries. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: The Sun stands at 19.3° Aries, in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best. Of everything the chart can be read for without a birth time, that is the loudest single fact in it.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: At noon on that date the Sun stood at 19.3° Aries, inside the second decan (10°–20°), whose traditional sub-ruler is the Sun. The decan is the older, finer division — it is what the sign looks like once you stop rounding it to thirty degrees.

blocks.title: The fast planets
blocks.text: For the fast movers, Mercury was at 4.5° Taurus, Venus was at 3.5° Gemini, Mars was at 15.1° Capricorn. Read together: thought with its feet on the ground; attraction that begins as conversation; effort banked steadily until it tells.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Mercury and Uranus hold the closest angle here — a opposition, 0.2° wide. An opposition puts two needs on opposite shores of the same water. Neither drowns; neither gets the whole beach. Behind it, Neptune conjunction Pluto at 0.3°, and Jupiter sextile Neptune at 1.5° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. All of it stands whatever the hour was: each angle was tested from midnight to midnight before it was written down.

blocks.title: Figures in the geometry
blocks.text: The Moon makes no major aspect that survives the day; the old reading gives such a planet autonomy — it acts alone, sometimes loudly.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: Read against the old dignities, two placements stand out. The Sun in Aries at 19.3° is in exaltation — the tradition’s honoured-guest placement, working at its best; Mars in Capricorn at 15.1° is in exaltation. None of this ranks anyone; dignity describes footing, and footing can be worked with.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Of the 10 placements whose signs hold for the whole day: 4 in earth, 3 in air, 2 in fire, 1 in water by element, 5 mutable, 3 cardinal, 2 fixed by modality. An earth emphasis reads as trust in the tangible: the plan matters less than whether the thing stands up. Saturn and Uranus were retrograde — the optical reversal the tradition reads as review — energy turned over before it is turned out.

blocks.title: The Moon, and how far it can move
blocks.text: The Moon stayed in Virgo for the whole of that day at the birthplace, covering 12.0° between midnight and midnight. That is quick enough to make the exact degree a neighbourhood rather than an address, and slow enough to leave the sign settled. At the noon reference it stands at 10.6°.
